text:
maya: heads-up customer on mobile webview (Android) behind an http/2 corporate proxy seeing garbled streaming output and occasional duplicate partial tokens. repro on Chrome webview + vpn.
eli: any logs or captures?
maya: pasted a tiny server-side stream dump we captured while reproducing: 
```
2026-03-23T12:08:01.100Z OUT chunk="data: {\"id\":1,\"seq\":0,\"text\":\"He\"}\n"
2026-03-23T12:08:01.101Z OUT chunk="data: {\"id\":2,\"seq\":0,\"text\":\"This is id2\"}\n"
2026-03-23T12:08:01.102Z OUT chunk="data: {\"id\":1,\"seq\":1,\"text\":\"llo\"}\n"
```
maya: proxy seems to multiplex frames and the webview reader sometimes yields these chunks out-of-order or with extra empty frames in-between. sampleapp's client simply splits on "\n\n" and emits events in read order -> we end up with id2 emitted before id1 reconstructed, which breaks downstream ordering assumptions and sometimes causes duplicate concatenation when reconnection occurs.
sam: is this unique to webview? Node/browser desktop behave differently?
maya: node SDK and desktop chrome use slightly different fetch impls and ended up buffering more before emitting. webview's fetch/read loop yields smaller slices and interleaving shows up. parity gap.
eli: any crashes or just wrong order?
maya: mainly wrong order and duplicated partial tokens when reconnect logic retries. Example from client console: `HeThis is id2llo` and downstream JSON.parse throws when objects get concatenated without delimiters.
jonah: auth/retry complicates this: when token refresh triggers reconnect, server may resume producing chunks that include a resume comment or token. some clients append leftover buffer from old conn into new stream without clearing incremental parsers, so fragments from before reconnect get merged with fragments after reconnect.
rachel: i prototyped a small repro harness that simulates http/2 interleaving by shuffling chunk order and injecting blank chunks. naive client impl: 
```js
const r = await fetch(url);
const reader = r.body.getReader();
let buf = '';
while(true){
  const {done, value} = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  buf += new TextDecoder().decode(value);
  const events = buf.split('\n\n');
  events.slice(0,-1).forEach(e => handle(e));
  buf = events[events.length-1];
}
```
rachel: naive approach assumes read-order == logical order. when chunks for multiple ids interleave, this breaks.
sam: proposed robust approach: include short per-event sequence metadata (you already have seq), client should reassemble fragments keyed by event id + seq, buffering out-of-order fragments up to a configurable window (e.g., 100 events) and emit when contiguous. Also, treat empty events as no-op. On reconnect, if server emits a `:resume <token>` comment we should call parser.reset() only if token changes, otherwise attempt gap-fill based on resume token.
eli: agree. smaller immediate steps: 1) make client tolerant of empty frames and drop them, 2) stop treating read-order as canonical ordering, instead parse event-level metadata (id/seq) when available and buffer keyed by id until complete, 3) on auth-refresh/reconnect, expose an explicit server-sent resume marker and have client reset or reconcile buffer based on token.
jonah: we should also harden TextDecoder usage: use streaming decode as others suggested to avoid UTF-8 split errors (TextDecoder.decode(chunk, {stream:true}) + finalize at done).
maya: customer also saw repeated timeouts because webview's read loop returned empty reads before network stabilized and our client treated that as disconnect -> we should debounce transient empty-read events and only consider done=true as final.
sam: ok i'll sketch a tiny parser utility we can share across browser/node/sdk: API: createOrderedSseParser({onEmit, onComment, maxBufferWindow}) with methods feed(bytes) and resetOnResume(token). It will: streaming-decode, split into raw events, parse id+seq if present, buffer fragments keyed by id, assemble when seqs contiguous, drop blank events, and optionally reset or reconcile on resume token. Keep it small and opt-in for now.
rachel: will add an integration test harness that shuffles chunks, injects blank frames, splits utf8 multi-byte sequences, and simulates resume tokens. Run across webview+chrome and node.
ci-bot: sampleapp-integration/webview-sse-reorder matrix queued (win-android-webview, linux-desktop, node).
devx-bot: created RDW-3005: "webview: SSE reassembly for out-of-order/http2-multiplexed chunks + resume-safe parser" and assigned to sam + rachel.
maya: customer provided workaround (force single connection/pinned http1), but they want upstream fix. i'll update them with issue and ETA.
eli: small docs note for sampleapp readme about proxies, http/2 multiplexing, and resume semantics would help onboarding. add reproduction snippet and troubleshooting tips.
sam: will open PR with parser util, unit+e2e tests, and README blurb. will start with a small opt-in opt for sampleapp to reduce risk. aiming to land in next patch. :rocket:
